1995.kid: The laptop’s phone calls the internet company, by radio to the mast. The call gets its own seat in the radio waves, a tiny moment that comes round again and again, and keeps it until you hang up. It’s slow, and every minute costs money.
1995.nerd: GSM circuit-switched data (CSD): a full-rate traffic channel, TCH/F9.6, one time slot of eight on a 200 kHz carrier around 900 MHz, yours for the whole call. 12 kbit/s of RLP frames (resent when garbled) coded to 22.8 kbit/s on air; 9.6 kbit/s left for PPP. Billed per minute, like a call.
